title: Amazon VPC
description: Learn how to build a Virtual Private Cloud with subnets, route tables, IGW, NAT Gateway, security groups, and NACLs.

data.text: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a logically isolated section of the AWS cloud where you can launch AWS resources. Within a VPC, you control your virtual networking environment: you select your IP address range, create subnets, and configure route tables and network gateways.

data.title: Your Private Network in the Cloud
data.text: Think of a VPC as your own private data center inside AWS. You decide which parts are public-facing and which parts stay private, and you control all traffic entering and leaving.
A VPC consists of several key components that work together to define your network.

data.title: Core VPC Components
items: CIDR Block — The IP address range for your VPC (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16).
Subnets — Ranges of IP addresses within your VPC. Subnets can be public or private.
Internet Gateway (IGW) — Connects your VPC to the internet.
Route Tables — Rules that determine where network traffic is directed.
NAT Gateway — Allows private subnet instances to access the internet while remaining private.
Security Groups — Virtual firewalls for instances at the instance level.
Network ACLs (NACLs) — Optional firewalls at the subnet level with stateless rules.

data.text: A public subnet has a route to an Internet Gateway and can directly communicate with the internet. A private subnet does not have a route to the Internet Gateway. Instances in private subnets are isolated from the internet and can only receive inbound traffic through a NAT Gateway or other proxy.

terms.definition: Virtual Private Cloud — a logically isolated network you control within AWS.
A range of IP addresses within a VPC, usually divided by Availability Zone.
A horizontally scaled VPC component that allows communication between your VPC and the internet.
A managed service that allows private subnet instances to access the internet without being directly reachable.
A stateful virtual firewall that controls traffic at the instance level.
An optional stateless firewall that controls traffic at the subnet level.

data.title: Create a VPC with AWS CLI
data.content: This example creates a VPC, a public subnet, an Internet Gateway, and a route table.
data.code:
# Create a VPC with a /16 CIDR block
aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.0.0.0/16

# Create a public subnet in us-east-1a
aws ec2 create-subnet \
  --vpc-id vpc-12345678 \
  --cidr-block 10.0.1.0/24 \
  --availability-zone us-east-1a

# Create and attach an Internet Gateway
aws ec2 create-internet-gateway
aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway \
  --vpc-id vpc-12345678 \
  --internet-gateway-id igw-12345678

# Create a route table and route traffic to the IGW
aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id vpc-12345678
aws ec2 create-route \
  --route-table-id rtb-12345678 \
  --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 \
  --gateway-id igw-12345678

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: A VPC is your isolated private network in the AWS cloud
Subnets divide your VPC into public and private zones
Internet Gateways connect public subnets to the internet
NAT Gateways let private instances access the internet safely
Security Groups and NACLs provide layered firewall protection
data.takeaway: Next, you will learn how to connect VPCs, use VPC peering, Transit Gateway, and Direct Connect.
